title: ExecutionEngineRegistry
description: Registry of Execution Engines that may consume an APPROVED EngineeringProposal (docs/cad-skills/contracts/proposal.schema.json). An Execution Engine owns only execution - it does not own the Prompt Compiler, Loop Engine, Skills, Proposal compilation, or Approval. This mirrors docs/cad-skills/registry/skill-registry.schema.json's registry-wrapper pattern deliberately, so the same JSONSchemaValidator already used by docs/cad-skills/tests/test_cad_skills.py can validate both without new validator code. As of the Engineering Hardening pass, execution-engines.json (validated against this schema) is read at runtime by the 'execute' CLI command (validateExecutionEngine in .claude/loop/loop-trace.mjs), which refuses an engineId not present in this registry.

vendor.description: Repository-evidenced vendor attribution only. Use 'Not specified by repository documentation' rather than inferring an unverified vendor - see prompt-compiler's own 'must not silently invent facts' rule (.claude/skills/prompt-compiler/SKILL.md).

capabilities.description: Capabilities this engine is confirmed, by repository evidence, to have available. Do not list a capability the engine has not been observed to exercise in this repository - an untested capability belongs in 'limitations', not here.

limitations.description: Known gaps, untested claims, or structural constraints for this engine, stated plainly rather than omitted.

verificationLevel.description: Same evidence-strength tiering already used by .claude/loop/loop-trace.mjs's computeVerifyVerdict (confirmedByHook vs confirmedByExplicitLog), generalized to describe the engine's invocation-evidence ceiling rather than a single invocation's evidence.

notes.description: Free-text evidence citation for why this engine's capabilities/status were classified this way. Required, not optional, so no engine entry can assert a status without a stated basis.
